q2: Partly. L1934 does not hold up in context. Joyce proposed that the CMS create button pushes rep information to Salesforce. Straight after that, Kobi said reps must be Salesforce users created through an admin task. Joyce replied 'That's a really good point' and asked whether the step was still needed. Strahinja said 'there might need to be some sort of manual workload'. The workflow they settled on is L1936: create the Salesforce user first, then the CMS sends its unique ID and the records match by email. Emily summarised it as 'Salesforce first we create the account there... once the rep's created on the CMS it'll send the unique ID to match them by email.' So on 2026-08-18 the only agreed automated part was the CMS sending the external ID back by email match, not CMS-driven rep creation. The claim's statement that 'creating a rep in the CMS is the event that pushes rep information to Salesforce' overstates the decision. L1961 only confirms that the external ID field is needed for mapping. It says nothing about how the field gets populated.

It lists automated CMS-to-Salesforce sync as a future possibility and puts it out of scope. WAGR-183's 2026-08-25 comment ('all user fields are generally going to be set manually during user provisioning') matches this. The only gap: the WAGR-183 description bullet 'BAs are created upstream via the CMS, same as Player' is stale and conflicts with WAGR-390. That is a documentation cleanup, not a scope variance.
